items.headline: Run of US outages (Microsoft, FAA, Chase, NSA network, Apple) – officials say no cyberattack, cite upgrades and patching
items.summary: Five unrelated-looking US outages in 12 days, including a four-hour-plus nationwide FAA ground stop, drew questions about cyberattack. DNI, DHS and FBI told Congress they see no coordinated or malicious cause; each organisation cites a software bug, router upgrade or patch.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: The outages are confirmed by the affected organisations (FAA, NSA, Apple, Microsoft, Chase) and multiple outlets. The cause of each, and the 'no cyberattack' finding, are the organisations' and officials' own statements; no independent forensic verification has been published.

sections.happened: Over 12 days the US saw several unrelated-looking outages. Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot) failed worldwide on 12 Nov for nearly 24 hours. On 13 Nov the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop from about 20:30 GMT; the FAA says traffic resumed about 01:15 GMT, and it counts about 12,462 cancelled flights. On 16 Nov JPMorgan Chase online banking, payments and some branch systems were disrupted, with knock-on effects at other banks and Zelle. On 17 Nov the NSA's internal NSANet degraded, staggering staff arrivals, and Apple services including iCloud, Apple Pay and the App Store failed from about 17:45 GMT. On 18 Nov officials told a House committee they see no coordinated or malicious cause.
sections.technical: Causes differ per incident. FAA: legacy equipment destabilised when data flooded its FTI network at 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds, hitting 17 of 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers; L3Harris was replacing copper with fibre and deploying Juniper routers at El Dorado, Arkansas (a radar site in Amarillo, Texas was also named). Microsoft: a July gateway software bug, extra Teams failover traffic and about 14% of capacity already offline; over 80% of servers became unresponsive. Chase: a software release (FBI official via Fox Business). NSA: DNI Jay Clayton cited PHP patching; NSA said 'routine maintenance'. Apple: 'an internal update'. No CVEs, malware, actors or IOCs are attributed.
sections.guidance: FAA said it disabled the functionality on the originating Juniper routers and on more than 60 others, and paused installing them. Microsoft said it added capacity, monitoring and safeguards. Secretary Mullin said DHS would call private-sector representatives about notifying customers before upgrades. CBS reported FBI, NSA and CISA urged immediate PHP patching on 21 Oct.
sections.differing: Mullin said he is '98 percent' sure there was no cyberattack and floated AI, citing an unnamed tech contact. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford, per TechCrunch, cited 'zero evidence' of AI involvement; Microsoft said AI agents were not the cause. Duffy blamed routine maintenance; the FAA said legacy TDM equipment, not upgrades, was responsible, then paused the Juniper rollout.
sections.unknown: The FAA root cause is still under investigation by the FAA and L3Harris. Microsoft's final report is pending. Whether the Chase, Apple and NSA events share any cause is unconfirmed; Apple has published no detailed cause.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway root-RCE flaw CVE-2026-76466 exploited against a Russian organisation after public PoC, F6 reports
items.summary: Russian firm F6 says attackers used the critical Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) against a Russian company soon after a public exploit appeared. Cisco's advisory, unrevised since 21 October, still says it knows of no exploitation.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: The flaw, CVSS 9.8 and fix are confirmed in Cisco's own advisory. The exploitation claim rests on one incident-response vendor (F6); Cisco has not confirmed it and no independent source or victim has corroborated it.

sections.happened: Cisco published advisory cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t on 21 October 2026 (16:00 GMT, 17:00 UK) for CVE-2026-76466, crediting Stefan Aleksic of Jane Street. A public exploit and detector were posted on GitHub by researcher Nicolas Krassas (reported by Cyberpress on 12 November). On 18 November F6 said it investigated the first exploitation case, at an unnamed Russian company, shortly after the PoC appeared. F6 named no actor and no victim. SecurityWeek (19 November) says it has asked Cisco for comment.
sections.technical: Unauthenticated remote root command execution on clustered Expressway-C/-E (virtual and appliance); CVSS 3.1 9.8, CWE-798, bug CSCww27732. Fixed in X15.5.20; X15.5.3 and earlier affected. F6: attackers compromised two internet-facing X15.5.3 nodes, then two internal cluster nodes, and ran custom Python scripts for network scanning, SMB, SQL Server, WinRM and GitLab searching, edited during the attack; code comments suggested an AI assistant. Indicators from F6: IPs 66.179.31[.]32, 18.130.47[.]116; erlang.log entry nodeup,'wombat@127.0.0.1'; paths /mnt/harddisk/i{0-9}{4}[a-zA-Z]?/*.py. No ATT&CK IDs published.
sections.guidance: Cisco: X15.5.20 resolves the flaw; no workarounds exist; X14 and earlier customers must migrate to a fixed release. F6: if updating is not possible, restrict TCP 4371–4372 at the firewall to trusted cluster-node IPs, and check erlang.log for the indicator above.
sections.differing: Cisco's advisory attributes the flaw to persistent cookies plus unvalidated client certificates when TLS Verify Mode is Enabled. The PoC author describes a hard-coded maintenance identity and cookie, working in Permissive mode, the stated default; Cisco's CWE-798 classification fits hard-coded credentials. Cisco's advisory says no malicious use known; F6 reports exploitation. Advisory still version 1.0.
sections.unknown: Victim identity, actor, initial access date, whether F6's AI-assistant inference is correct, other victims, Cisco's response, and CISA KEV status (not verified).

items.headline: Suspected Chinese APT rebuilds EggStreme malware after Bitdefender exposure
items.summary: Bitdefender's update says a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt its EggStreme malware after its September 2025 report, adding passive backdoors and new protocols while targeting Philippine government organisations.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Vendor research update; victims unnamed, no government acknowledgement, attribution only suspected.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026 (UK time), Bitdefender blog update; reported same day by Infosecurity Magazine and The Hacker News

sections.happened: Bitdefender's 18 November 2026 update to its September 2025 research says a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt EggStreme after exposure; the timing suggests the report was a likely trigger. It assesses with high confidence that multiple Philippine government organisations were targeted. Taiwan targeting is low-to-medium confidence. No new attribution claim.
sections.technical: EggStremeFuel changed configuration protection 12 days after the report; the loader's cipher changed about two weeks later. EggStremeAgent moved to raw TCP with mutual TLS; newer builds drop the keylogger and some run passive listeners. DLL sideloading, file-share movement and in-memory execution persist.
sections.guidance: Bitdefender recommends restricting unneeded built-in Windows tools, detecting DLL sideloading by library name and location, finding unmanaged machines reaching workstations, and watching for new inbound listeners.
sections.differing: Bitdefender says timing suggests its report prompted the changes; some builds predate it, so causation is unconfirmed. Overlap with Palo Alto's CL-STA-1048 is not established.
sections.unknown: Initial access is undetermined; victims unnamed, no count published; Taiwan targeting is a lead; EggStremeWizard status unclear.

items.headline: Equinor confirms ongoing cyber-attack on certain IT systems; production unaffected
items.summary: Norway's largest gas supplier Equinor says an ongoing cyber-attack hit some IT systems. Production is unaffected and no data theft is indicated. No group has been named.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company statement on its own website, updated 18 and 19 November 2026.
items.firstReported: 17 November 2026, 17:55 UK time (18:55 CET), Equinor statement on equinor.com

sections.happened: Equinor said on 17 November 2026 it had detected an ongoing cyber-attack against certain IT systems. Its 18 November update said the attack was not a virus. The 19 November update said it was still ongoing, production was normal, no data theft was indicated, and the matter had been reported to police.
sections.technical: Equinor has not disclosed the attack vector, initial access, affected systems, malware or indicators of compromise. It states the attack is not a virus and so carries no risk of spreading.
sections.differing: Reuters, citing a source, and NTB report internal email and applications were disrupted. Equinor says operations and production are unaffected and does not say whether operational technology systems were reached.
sections.unknown: Attack duration, scope, access route, responsible party and whether data was accessed. Equinor says it is too early to say how long recovery will take.

items.headline: Optimizely platform abused to inject malicious JavaScript into 178 top websites
items.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely Experimentation on 16 November 2026 to inject malicious JavaScript into customer projects, reaching at least 178 sites including BBC, CNN and Zoom.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Optimizely confirmed incident; 178-site count is researcher Report URI's. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026, Report URI first identified the injection (BBC timeline from 02:21 UTC, injected version 04:21 UTC per Malwarebytes); UK time equals UTC in November

sections.happened: Optimizely said it identified a security incident on 16 November 2026 in which an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. Report URI counted 178 affected organisations, including BBC, CNN and Zoom. Optimizely says the vulnerability is fixed.
sections.technical: Supply-chain injection through a third-party JavaScript snippet. Payload was rebuilt 26 times in a day; it steals payment card data, cookies and screenshots, swaps cryptocurrency addresses, and delivers DarkSword and Coruna iOS/iPadOS exploit kits. No CVE or ATT&CK IDs published.
sections.guidance: Optimizely lists remediation steps: blocking the vulnerable path, removing injected code, ending sessions, revoking tokens, resetting affected accounts. Report URI's Scott Helme advises content security policies.
sections.differing: Report URI says the injected files were clean by 23:11 UTC on 16 November. Malwarebytes notes its BBC timeline does not establish that BBC servers were breached.
sections.unknown: Exploited vulnerability, root cause and attacker identity are not public. Optimizely's third-party investigation is ongoing. Full list of affected sites is Report URI's.

items.headline: Google reports Star Blizzard (Cold Relic) chaining cloud identity compromises across US organisations
items.summary: Google researchers describe Russian group Star Blizzard, aka Cold Relic, using stolen cloud super-admin and SSO identities to steal data and pivot to a second US organisation.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Google GTIG/Mandiant report; victims unnamed; primary page unreadable to us. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (Google blog date); Infosecurity Magazine 18 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated)

sections.happened: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant published analysis of two linked intrusions at US organisations. A late-2025 Google Workspace super-admin compromise used MFA push fatigue and a residential proxy; data was bulk-exported and access persisted for months. A 2026 intrusion used Entra ID SSO credentials obtained via a messaging-app impersonation. Google says activity continued in November 2026.
sections.technical: Initial access via stolen super-admin credentials and MFA fatigue (T1621), residential proxies, and phishing links for Entra ID credentials and tokens. Persistence via rogue MFA devices, passkeys and backup codes. Collection via Takeout and bulk drive downloads; Alert Center notifications deleted. CVEs, malware and IOCs: none reported.
sections.guidance: Google recommends enriching authentication logs with residential proxy and VPN reputation feeds, conditional access blocking known proxies, cloud DLP policies, phishing-resistant MFA, restricting passkey registration, and revoking all sessions and resetting passwords after intrusion.
sections.differing: Google attributes the group to Russian state intelligence; the DOJ is reported as assessing it operates within the FSB. Vendor-neutral sources repeat this; no differing accounts found.
sections.unknown: Victim organisations, sectors and total number affected are not named. Scale of the wider campaign and the full Microsoft-documented 2026 phishing expansion are not detailed in sources reviewed.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities discloses test-environment breach affecting up to 15.72 million accounts
items.summary: Japanese broker Rakuten Securities says customer data in a test environment may have leaked. Up to 4.47 million accounts had personal and financial details exposed; passwords and PINs reportedly not taken.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company's own 17 Nov notice, reported by multiple outlets; primary page not accessible. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (JST; UK time not stated), Rakuten Securities public notice; NHK WORLD, Jiji and Reuters covered it the same day

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities detected possible unauthorised access to part of its systems on 16 November and cut access. Its 17 November notice says test-environment data may have leaked on 11 November. Up to 11.25 million accounts had login IDs and branch codes exposed; up to 4.47 million also had personal and financial details. Total up to 15.72 million.
sections.technical: Production customer data sat in a test environment. Attack vector, CVEs and ATT&CK IDs not published; company says cause still under investigation. Mallory reports an undisclosed vulnerability was exploited, unverified.
sections.guidance: Company warns of fake emails, texts, calls posing as it or affiliates; says its emails contain no links. Passkey (FIDO2) login is to become mandatory; a settings option temporarily freezes trading and withdrawals.
sections.differing: Media total 15.72 million. ASCII.jp cites a spokesperson saying the categories do not overlap; DEV Community argues the sum double-counts. Sources cannot settle which is correct; the figures are stated as maximums.
sections.unknown: Attacker, intrusion method, root cause, why production data was in test, whether data actually left systems, regulator reporting, and any account misuse.

items.headline: Wellington IT breach exposes payee data at about 40 Irish credit unions
items.summary: Belfast-based IT supplier Wellington IT confirmed a cyber incident affecting its CU Online banking platform. Payee records at about 40 Irish credit unions were exposed; the attack ran 2–4 October 2026.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Supplier confirmed incident; several credit unions published notices; scope still unverified. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 onwards; credit union notices from 17 Nov; first public report BleepingComputer 18 Nov 2026, 14:39 UK time (article timestamp is 02:39 PM, presumed UK)

sections.happened: Wellington IT, a Belfast-based supplier serving about 50 credit unions (43 in Ireland), was hit by an attack on 2–4 October 2026. An automated script made about five million requests to exploit an authorisation flaw and accessed private records using valid credentials. Notices to members came mid-November; the minister called the delay not acceptable.
sections.technical: Reported as an authorisation flaw in the CU Online platform, abused via valid credentials and an automated script (five million requests). Cavan Credit Union's notice, as reported by iThome, says the flaw was patched on 6 October 2026. Exposed payee fields: name, nickname, IBAN, BIC, account number, sort code, address, payment reference. No activity logs to confirm which records were taken.
sections.guidance: Members advised to remain vigilant for phishing and impersonation attempts. Credit unions say passwords, PINs, card details and online banking credentials were not affected.
sections.differing: Wellington IT says the investigation is ongoing and scope unconfirmed. The minister says no financial loss has been identified so far. Credit unions differ on whether core banking was accessed: Ballincollig says it was not.
sections.unknown: Total number of affected individuals; whether data was taken or only accessed; the full list of affected credit unions; attacker identity.

items.headline: TfL says about 265,000 Oyster photocard customers' account details may be compromised; photocard website offline
items.summary: TfL says unauthorised emails from its own system on 16 November exposed a compromise of its photocard portal. About 265,000 customers' contact details, dates of birth and security answers may be affected; TfL reports no passwords or payment data. ICO informed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: TfL, through a named director (Shashi Verma), acknowledged the compromise and the 265,000 figure to BBC, The Register and Infosecurity Magazine; TfL's own notice text was read only as quoted by outlets. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Wed 18 Nov 2026, evening UK time (BBC, syndicated 20:49 GMT); TfL became aware Mon 16 Nov (time not stated)

sections.happened: On Monday 16 November 2026 TfL became aware that Oyster photocard customers were receiving emails, sent from TfL's own system, asking them to create accounts they already held. TfL said the emails were generated as a result of the compromise. It took the photocard website down, which remained offline on 19 November. On 18 November it said about 265,000 customers may have had account details compromised, began contacting them, and notified the ICO. Affected card types include Zip Oyster (ages 5-18), 18+ Student, 18-25 Care Leaver, 60+ London, Apprentice and Veterans. TfL says the incident is contained.
sections.technical: No attack vector, vulnerability, CVE, actor, malware or IOC has been published. The only indicator is the unauthorised emails, which TfL says originated from its own system, implying access to the account or mailing function of the photocard portal. Data TfL says was exposed: names, email and home addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, security questions and answers (BBC; ianVisits). TfL's current assessment: passwords, bank or payment card details, journey data, photo copies, and names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised.
sections.guidance: TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change their password and security question and answer, and advises changing the password on any other service using the same details. It says existing photocards remain valid for travel. Renewals and journey-history queries go through customer services (0343 222 1234), and top-ups work at ticket machines while the site is offline.
sections.differing: BBC reports the details were "accessed" and "compromised"; TfL's statement uses "may have had their account details compromised". TfL's own figure is an estimate that it says was "significantly reduced" by its speed of response. The Register says nothing at present suggests a link to the September 2024 attack; TfL has not publicly attributed this incident.
sections.unknown: Entry method, dwell time, who is responsible, whether data was copied or misused, the final number affected, and when the website returns are unstated. TfL's investigation is continuing.

items.headline: Microsoft's official agent-framework PyPI package hijacked: versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 carried a cloud and CI credential stealer
items.summary: Two malicious agent-framework releases (1.26.1, 1.26.2) appeared on PyPI on 17 November, about 33 minutes apart, running a credential stealer at every Python start. PyPI quarantined both within the hour; Microsoft confirmed removal and an investigation. How the upload was achieved is disputed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: A Microsoft Agent Framework maintainer confirmed in GitHub issue #10411 that the compromised versions were pulled and an investigation is under way; PyPI's quarantine is documented by StepSecurity, and Wiz, StepSecurity, OX Security, SafeDep, Endor Labs and Upwind independently analysed the wheels. Root cause is not confirmed by Microsoft.

sections.happened: On 17 November 2026 two releases of Microsoft's official `agent-framework` package on PyPI, 1.26.1 (20:35 GMT) and 1.26.2 (21:08 GMT), carried a credential stealer. StepSecurity records PyPI quarantining 1.26.1 at 21:06 and 1.26.2 at 21:16; Wiz reports both unavailable by about 21:30. The last clean release, 1.26.0, dates from 12 November. Upwind Security opened a GitHub issue; a Microsoft maintainer replied that the versions were pulled and an investigation was under way. OX Security puts the package at about 192,000 downloads a month; installs of the bad versions are not published. Wiz, StepSecurity, OX, Socket, SafeDep, Endor Labs and Aikido published analyses.
sections.technical: Wheel-only uploads to the official project (ATT&CK T1195.002; IDs here are editorial, not vendor-published). Each wheel adds a `.pth` startup hook (T1546.018) running at every Python start without importing the package: `agent_framework_meta.pth` in 1.26.1, `af_runtime_diag.pth` in 1.26.2. The payload collects environment variables, credential files and up to 300 other processes' environments (T1552.001), and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps OIDC and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens (T1552.005, T1528). It sends one zlib/base64 POST to a webhook.site URL (T1567). Researchers found no second stage. No CVE; no actor attributed. Hashes and IOCs are in the StepSecurity, Wiz and Upwind posts.
sections.guidance: PyPI quarantined both versions; StepSecurity and Wiz identify 1.26.0 as the last clean release. The Microsoft maintainer said the versions were pulled from the feed. Wiz, StepSecurity, OX and Upwind published remediation steps: isolate hosts before running Python or pip, remove hook files, rebuild, rotate reachable credentials, audit OIDC and managed-identity trust. Upwind notes `_AF_TEL=1` blocks execution.
sections.differing: Wiz: the attacker appears to have compromised a Microsoft ESRP release-pipeline certificate and key; a first upload from AWS was rejected, a second from Microsoft IP space succeeded. Upwind: likely a compromised PyPI upload credential. SafeDep: a PyPI maintainer `vibiret`, created 17 November, is a suspected uploader, unconfirmed. Microsoft has confirmed none. Wiz's account draws on attacker tooling telemetry.
sections.unknown: Microsoft has not published a root cause or said whether upload access is revoked. Victim total unknown: Wiz saw three unique victim exfiltrations among 50 retained requests; later ones went unlogged. Microsoft made some repositories private; no link is established.

items.headline: CISA adds Perforce Puppet report-deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-115731, CVSS 9.4) to KEV; fixes issued 3 November
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731, a CVSS 9.4 deserialization flaw letting a CA-signed Puppet agent run code on Puppet Server, to its KEV catalogue on 17 November. Perforce and OpenVox patched on 3 November; a public PoC exists. Exploitation details are unpublished.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: CISA's KEV listing (17 Nov 2026, as quoted by The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and Help Net Security) records active exploitation, and Perforce, OpenVox and the finder (Neodyme) each published advisories or write-ups on the flaw and fixes. The CISA and Perforce pages could not be opened directly; their content is taken from those secondary quotations.

sections.happened: Neodyme AG researcher Alain Rödel reported CVE-2026-115731 and CVE-2026-115732 to Perforce and OpenVox in mid-October. Fixes and advisories were released on 3 November 2026 at 17:00 UTC (Neodyme). A Reddit user reported on 4 November a CA intrusion that used the flaw (as relayed by The Hacker News and SecurityWeek). OpenVox's advisory contains a proof-of-concept report. CISA added the CVE to KEV on Tuesday 17 November, with a federal civilian agency due date of 1 December. SecurityWeek's article (10:37 GMT, 18 November) was the earliest in this set. No actor, victims or scale have been published.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-115731: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data in Puppet report processing, CVSS 4.0 9.4 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L). An agent PUTs a report to /puppet/v3/report on port 8140; a crafted event with a __ptype rich-data type reaches class_eval and runs Ruby as the Puppet Server service user (OpenVox advisory, Neodyme). Needs any CA-signed agent certificate; autosign without strong verification lets unauthenticated attackers obtain one. Code execution exposes the CA signing key. Affected: Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.0–2023.8.12, 2025.0.0–2025.12.0, 2026.0.0; Puppet Core 8.x before 8.22.2, 9.0.0–9.1.2; OpenVox Server before 8.18.0/9.2.0. Companion CVE-2026-115732 (CVSS 9.0) is a certificate-name authorization bypass. No ATT&CK mapping or IOCs published; behaviour fits T1190.
sections.guidance: Perforce says customers should upgrade to Puppet Enterprise/Advanced 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13, or Puppet Core 9.1.3 or 8.22.2, and restart the server; if unable, review autosign configuration and authorization rules (Perforce, as quoted by Help Net Security). OpenVox fixed versions: Agent 9.3.0/8.32.0, Server 9.2.0/8.18.0. Red Hat's entry advises avoiding autosigning without strong verification.
sections.differing: Security Affairs and SC Media say no active exploitation is confirmed; Security Affairs attributes to Perforce a statement that it knows of no attacks, which could not be verified. The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and Help Net Security report CISA cited exploitation. KEV inclusion requires evidence of exploitation, so that is better supported. Outlets cite different BODs (26-04, 22-01).
sections.unknown: Who is exploiting the flaw, how many servers were compromised, and what CISA's evidence is remain unpublished. The 4 November Reddit report is a single anonymous post (page blocked to the researcher). Perforce's advisory text was not directly readable.

items.headline: Apache confirms active exploitation of critical Roller XML-RPC deserialization flaw (CVE-2026-129448)
items.summary: Apache says CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated XML-RPC deserialization flaw in Roller 4.0.0–6.1.4, is being exploited. It is the same bug as September's CVE-2026-82384, which listed only 6.1.5. Fixed in 6.1.6; no attack details published.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: The Apache Software Foundation's own advisory (17 November 2026) states the issue is being actively exploited and gives the CVSS score and affected versions; three outlets report the same. Apache has published no exploitation details.

sections.happened: On 17 November 2026 (about 11:02 UTC, per Corgea's timeline) Apache published CVE-2026-129448 for Apache Roller, a Java blogging server, covering versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and stated the issue is being actively exploited. Apache said it is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, announced on 25 September 2026 with only Roller 6.1.5 listed as affected. Credit: n0mi1k (finder), Matt Raible (reporter). Apache has not said who is exploiting the flaw, how, or how many servers are compromised. SecurityWeek reported CISA added a different Apache flaw (Axis, CVE-2026-90436) to its KEV catalogue that Wednesday, not this one. Roller 6.1.7 was released on 11 November with fixes for 15 other CVEs (SecurityWeek).
sections.technical: CVE-2026-129448 / CVE-2026-82384: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data, CVSS 3.1 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N), per Apache's September notice. Apache says the XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester. Corgea's analysis (secondary) says the servlet at /roller-services/xmlrpc was configured with enabledForExtensions=true, allowing an ex:serializable Java object; code execution depends on gadget classes on the classpath. Corgea reports a public Python proof-of-concept repository has existed since 28 September. The fix is merged in apache/roller PR #171. No IOCs, actor, malware or ATT&CK mapping published by Apache; the technique corresponds to T1190.
sections.guidance: Apache's advisory says users should upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the feature is disabled. Its stated workaround: set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, then restart Roller. Apache states disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough on older versions.
sections.differing: Version scope differs between sources. Apache's November notice lists 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, with 6.1.5 covered by the earlier CVE-2026-82384; Tuskira's advisory summarises the range as 4.0.0 through 6.1.5. Tuskira and Corgea reported it was not in CISA KEV at 17 November; SecurityWeek's KEV reference concerns Axis only.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, targets, payloads and number of compromised servers are unpublished. It is unclear when exploitation began and whether the September public PoC was used. Roller's install base is unstated. Apache's list pages did not render directly.

items.headline: F5 discloses six critical BIG-IP flaws that can crash TMM and may allow remote code execution; hotfixes only
items.summary: F5's 18 November out-of-band notification lists six stack-based overflows in BIG-IP iRule and APM features, each rated CVSS 9.8, allowing unauthenticated TMM crashes and possible RCE. F5 reports no exploitation; fixes are engineering hotfixes.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: F5 published the advisories and CVE records itself (CNA); extracts of F5 advisory text and the CVE record read, plus two independent trade write-ups. F5 pages themselves render only via JavaScript.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, CVE records published 15:23 GMT (F5 out-of-band security notification K000164058)

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 F5 issued an out-of-band security notification (K000164058) with 22 advisories, 10 of them for NGINX. Six cover BIG-IP flaws rated CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) and 9.3 (v4.0): five iRule-command bugs and one APM bug. F5 says an unauthenticated remote attacker can terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM), disrupting traffic while it restarts, and may achieve remote code execution. The Hacker News reports that watchTowr's Sina Kheirkhah reported four and F5 found two internally. The advisories do not state exploitation. The CVE records were reserved on 10 November.
sections.technical: All six are CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflows in the data plane (F5: no control plane exposure), CVSS:3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N. Each needs a configured trigger on a virtual server. CVE-2026-123637: APM per-request policy with Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. CVE-2026-121805: PEM::subscriber iRule. CVE-2026-120292: HTTP profile plus MR::message route. CVE-2026-120285: HTTP profile plus PSC::ip_address. CVE-2026-116953: GENERICMESSAGE::route. CVE-2026-120722: DNS::scrape. Affected branches in the CVE record: BIG-IP 21.1.0, 17.5.0, 17.1.0; BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes 2.2 to 2.4. No actor, malware or IOCs reported.
sections.guidance: F5 states the fix is an engineering hotfix (for example BIGIP-21.1.0.4.0.19.3-ENG, BIGIP-17.5.1.11.0.61.12-ENG, BIGIP-17.1.3.7.0.21.4-ENG; BNK-2.4.2-, 2.3.4-, 2.2.5-EHF1), selected per K000164239, and lists no workaround. F5 says hotfixes carry less QA than scheduled releases and are offered without warranty, and that versions past End of Technical Support are not evaluated.
sections.differing: F5's advisory for CVE-2026-120722 lists BIG-IP CNF as not vulnerable, while its CVE record, updated 18 November, lists CNF as affected, per The Hacker News. Daily CyberSecurity states CNF is not affected, while The Hacker News lists CNF as affected for two other CVEs. F5 has not published a reconciliation in sources read.
sections.unknown: No exploitation reported; none of the CVEs were found in CISA's KEV catalogue. Exploit requests are described only as 'undisclosed'. Whether RCE is practical is untested publicly. Number of exposed systems is unreported. CNF affected status is unresolved.

items.headline: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): OpenJDK Base64 memory-corruption flaw patched after pre-disclosure leak; CISA issues alert, exploitation attempts reported
items.summary: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938, a heap overflow in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder, after a leak. Oracle and OpenJDK shipped fixes on 17 November and CISA issued an alert. Exploitation attempts are reported; no successful intrusions confirmed. RCE needs per-application work.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes and advisories; CISA, the Canadian Cyber Centre and CERT-EU issued alerts; Cisco, Red Hat, Keycloak, Atlassian and others published vendor advisories. VulnCheck independently reproduced the overflow. Pre-auth RCE in named products rests on Calif's own demonstrations.

sections.happened: Calif said on X on 17 November that it had found and reported a flaw it named Java4Shell and that details had leaked. Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixed builds at about 21:00 UTC (GreyNoise timeline); Calif published its write-up at about 21:13 UTC. The Canadian Cyber Centre alert is dated 20:27 UTC and CISA's alert 22:30 UTC. Oracle rates it CVSS 3.1 8.1 (High); Calif rates it CVSS 4.0 9.2 (Critical). Calif says it demonstrated unauthenticated RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, and authenticated RCE in five others. By 19 November GreyNoise, watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian reported probing and attempted exploitation; GreyNoise reported no successful intrusions.
sections.technical: Integer underflow in the HotSpot x86-64 AVX-512 Base64 decode intrinsic (java.util.Base64) gives an out-of-bounds heap write of 62 bytes with fixed content (CWE-122/787). It needs a CPU with AVX-512 VBMI/BW (Intel Ice Lake or later, AMD Zen 4 or later); ARM is unaffected. Affected: OpenJDK 17.0.6+, 21, 25, 27 and distributions built on them (Endor Labs: Java 8 and 11 standard builds not affected). Attacker-controlled Base64 must reach the decoder, e.g. HTTP Basic, JWT, SAML. Crash is trivial; RCE needs heap grooming plus an ASLR bypass per target (VulnCheck, Calif). Technique: exploit public-facing application (T1190). Fix: JDK-8393212. No actor attributed; scanning used a 'java4shell-recon' User-Agent (watchTowr).
sections.guidance: Oracle fixed builds: 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1 and 8u513 (performance), per CERT-EU. Amazon, Microsoft and Azul released patched builds (SecurityWeek). CISA urges immediate patching and lists temporary controls. Calif, VulnCheck and CERT-EU cite -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or -XX:UseAVX=2. Atlassian advises disabling AVX-512 for Data Center products pending patches; Cisco lists no workarounds; Keycloak 26.8 images were rebuilt.
sections.differing: Oracle (CVSS 3.1, high complexity) rates 8.1; Calif and Atlassian (for its products) rate 9.2. Calif says it achieved RCE in default configurations; VulnCheck and OX Security call RCE hard and narrow, requiring hardware, an exposed decoder and a tailored chain. Calif's video demonstrations, VulnCheck's exploit and Immersive's reported exploit support feasibility per application, not universal exploitation.
sections.unknown: How the pre-disclosure leak occurred. Whether any intrusion has succeeded. Calif's per-product exploit chains are unpublished. Cisco, Siemens and Atlassian patches are pending. Real-world exposed population is unquantified.

items.headline: NGINX2Root: five critical NGINX flaws (CVE-2026-123007 and four others) patched by F5; public PoC for the HTTP/2 bug
items.summary: F5 released NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 on 18 November fixing five flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, led by a decade-old HTTP/2 bug (CVE-2026-123007). Rapid7 published a proof of concept; no exploitation in the wild has been reported.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: F5 (the NGINX maintainer) and nginx.org published advisories, fixed releases and CVE records on 18 November; researchers Xint, Wiz and Rapid7 independently published technical write-ups, and Rapid7 and Censys published PoC material.

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 F5 and nginx.org published fixes for five NGINX vulnerabilities, collectively named NGINX2Root by Xint: CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-121810 and CVE-2026-113425. F5 scores each CVSS 4.0 9.2 (CVSS 3.1 8.1) and says they can allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the worker process. Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7 and Xint each report independent discovery. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007 in HTTP/2, has been present since NGINX 1.9.5 (2015). Xint's post went live at 15:07 UTC; the CVE record was published around 15:00 GMT per a secondary source. Rapid7 published a PoC for CVE-2026-123007. Wiz and Xint say they withheld full exploits. Censys reports about 74 million internet-facing web properties running affected versions.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-123007: when a stream is cancelled, unused send-window credit is returned without a cap, so a later unsigned check underflows and the TLS send path copies out of bounds on the heap (F5: CWE-191; Xint calls it an overflow). It needs HTTP/2 enabled only. CVE-2026-123633: HTTP/2 use-after-free (1.19.7+) when proxying under connection pressure. CVE-2026-121810: HTTP/3 use-after-free (1.25.0+). CVE-2026-123634: resolver use-after-free with variable-built proxy names and SSI or mirror subrequests. CVE-2026-113425: mail-proxy use-after-free (auth_http). Rapid7's chain needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic and a specific x86-64 glibc path. Xint chained it with an unpatched Linux SCTP kernel bug for container escape and host root. ATT&CK classes: T1190, T1611. No actor or IOCs published.
sections.guidance: F5 and nginx.org list fixes in NGINX Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, and NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 and 37.3.0.1. Per THN, Plus R34 to R36 have no fix listed. Xint, Wiz and CERT-EU state disabling HTTP/2 blocks only CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. F5 lists workarounds for two flaws. Per Qualys, Ubuntu and Debian had no fixed packages on 18 Nov.
sections.differing: Severity: F5 rates all five 9.2 (CVSS 4.0); nginx.org rates two major, three medium. ASLR: F5 says code execution needs ASLR disabled or bypassed; Wiz, Xint and Rapid7 demonstrated bypasses. Effort: Rapid7 reports about 128 GB of traffic; Censys reproduced the corrupted state with a 5.69 MB capture, not full code execution.
sections.unknown: No in-the-wild exploitation reported by F5, Rapid7, Wiz, Censys or CERT-EU; CISA KEV did not list it per THN. Timing of distribution, ingress-nginx and Plus R34 to R36 fixes is unclear. The SCTP kernel flaw has no fix yet.

items.headline: PHP releases 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 after 'critical' pre-announcement; changelog lists CVE-2026-115560 session RCE fix
items.summary: PHP published security releases for all supported branches on 19 November after warning the top severity was CRITICAL. The 8.5.13 changelog lists 17 GHSA-tracked fixes, including CVE-2026-115560, a session-handler RCE needing unusual configuration. No exploitation of it has been reported.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: PHP's own site published the 18 November pre-notice, the 19 November release entries (webmaster list post 14:04 UTC) and the PHP 8 ChangeLog naming CVE-2026-115560 as fixed in 8.5.13. Per-branch changelogs for 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36, and CVSS scores, could not be read.

sections.happened: PHP's security team posted a notice on 18 November 2026 announcing security releases for 19 November, 14:00-14:30 UTC, covering all supported versions with a highest severity of CRITICAL. The notice named no CVEs. PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 were then published; the release entries are stamped 14:00 UTC and the webmaster-list post is 14:04 UTC. The 8.5.13 changelog lists 17 GHSA-tracked security fixes, including CVE-2026-115560, which PHP disclosed on 23 October as an unpatched session-handling RCE with a configuration mitigation. The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and Security Affairs linked it to this release before publication. No exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 appears in the sources reviewed.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-115560 (GHSA-658j-r8rw-q6mx, "Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution"): per PHP's 23 October advisory, an application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, switch it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and leave session upload progress enabled. A third-party GitHub repository (googlesky) claims a working lab PoC (unauthenticated object injection to RCE, tested on php:8.4.27-apache); unverified. Other 8.5.13 entries with RCE wording: CVE-2026-129474, CVE-2026-129496, CVE-2026-126714. CVSS scores and per-CVE severities were not retrievable. Distinct from PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2, fixed 21 October).
sections.guidance: PHP's 23 October advisory suggested session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release; it said applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. PHP's 21 October advisory said workers must be restarted for that setting. PHP states 8.1 and older receive no upstream updates; 8.2 reaches end of life on 31 December 2026.
sections.differing: PHP's notice names no CVE; the 8.5.13 changelog lists CVE-2026-115560 but not which entry carries the CRITICAL rating. PHP Foundation executive director Elizabeth Barron told The Register in October the flaw needs a "very unlikely combination" not expected in practice; the googlesky repository claims a working lab exploit. Those claims address different questions (prevalence versus exploitability).
sections.unknown: Which fix carries PHP's CRITICAL rating, CVSS scores, per-branch changelogs for 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36, whether any of the 17 fixes is exploited, and how many installations use the affected configuration are unpublished.

items.headline: Ukraine and FBI arrest four suspects in ransomware extortion group linked to $40.5M in ransoms
items.summary: Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, arrested four suspected key members of a ransomware group that extorted over $40.5M from at least 28 companies using phone-based IT support impersonation.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Arrests announced by Ukrainian authorities; reported by three outlets; ransom totals are police claims. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (Wednesday), Prosecutor General's Office announcement as reported by The Record; UK time not stated in sources

sections.happened: Ukrainian police, with the FBI, arrested four suspected key members of a ransomware group. Acting National Police chief Maksym Tsutskiridze said at least 28 companies paid over $40.5M. 66 searches were held in Kyiv and 11 regions; the suspects are in custody.
sections.technical: Attackers impersonated IT support by phone, used an AI-generated voice platform, and tricked staff into giving credentials or installing TeamViewer/AnyDesk. Court records describe a fake corporate VPN login page and 2FA code capture. Police did not name the ransomware strain.
sections.differing: Court records, per LeMagIT and The Record, name Chaos as the ransomware; police did not name a strain. Links to Conti, BlackSuit or Royal are unconfirmed; police have not confirmed the suspects' Conti membership.
sections.unknown: Final damage total is still being established. Strain and group name are unconfirmed. Police say other network members are being identified.

items.headline: US interim rule requires export licences for AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil
items.summary: US Commerce interim final rule requires licences to ship advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, and restricts remote compute access by Chinese-linked firms.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Rule and Megaspeed probe reported by several outlets; primary text not read. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Mon 16 Nov 2026 (US time) per CNBC and Streamline Feed; Qz says Sunday. UK time not stated.

sections.happened: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule, effective 19 November 2026. It requires licences to ship covered advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, exempts US-headquartered companies, and restricts remote compute for Chinese-linked firms. Commerce and DOJ confirmed a criminal probe into Megaspeed.
sections.guidance: Public comments are invited under docket BIS-2026-0628 for 60 days after publication, per a secondary summary.
sections.differing: Malaysia says operators must comply and it will not negotiate. Singapore is studying the measure and seeks trusted access. China's Foreign Ministry calls it economic coercion. Analysts differ on impact.
sections.unknown: Effects on existing facilities, enforcement against non-compliant jurisdictions and the Megaspeed outcome remain unclear. Final rule text awaits comment.

items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first trilateral summit in Shenzhen and publish four-point 'Declaration toward Peace'
items.summary: The US, Chinese and Russian leaders met at Kylin Villa on 19 Nov and published a four-point declaration on UN reform, refined-fuel supply, ICC jurisdiction and nuclear-risk dialogue. It does not mention Ukraine or Iran; no concrete targets were given.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Declaration text published by Xinhua (Chinese state media), the Kremlin (per AFP) and the White House; wording matches across versions. Characterisations of the talks by individual governments are claims.
items.firstReported: 09:25 UK, 19 Nov 2026 (Japan Times); White House text posted 13:53 UK

sections.happened: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met at Kylin Villa, Shenzhen, on 19 November 2026 on the sidelines of the APEC leaders' meeting, the first meeting of the three together. Reports put the closed session at roughly 80–90 minutes. Xinhua and the Kremlin released the declaration first. AP reported the US had not yet released it; the White House then posted it at 13:53 UK time. No joint press statement followed. Trump had earlier met Xi and Putin separately.
sections.technical: The four-point declaration says: (1) China, Russia and the US, as UN Security Council permanent members, commit to UN reform; (2) the three plan to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products and affirm stable energy flows; (3) state consent and immunity of state officials are 'of paramount importance' and the International Criminal Court and similar bodies 'must not abuse their jurisdiction'; (4) a nuclear war 'cannot be won and must never be fought', with a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. No targets, dates or mechanisms are given.
sections.guidance: The White House and Xinhua each published the full declaration text. The White House version names Xi as 'State Chairman'; Xinhua's says 'President'. No implementation steps or follow-up meetings were published in the texts reviewed.
sections.differing: Ukraine: Trump said it was on the agenda and had been discussed with Putin; Kremlin spokesman Peskov said it was not the central topic; the declaration omits Ukraine and Iran. Xi's remarks, 'fruitful' description and Taiwan discussion come via Chinese state media and are claims. Putin's statements that the Crimean Bridge is civilian-only are Russian claims.
sections.unknown: How the dialogue on nuclear risks would be organised, and whether China will join arms-control talks. No ICC response was found. Ukraine and European governments' formal responses remain unclear.

items.headline: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83 per share, ahead of Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Anthropic priced its Nasdaq IPO at $83 per share, above its $70-78 range, selling 980 million shares for about $81.3 billion, a record. Trading as ANT was set for 19 November.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company press release and multiple major outlets report the same pricing figures.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026 (UK time, evening); first source Anthropic press release, anthropic.com

sections.happened: Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering at $83.00 per share on 18 November 2026, above the earlier $70-$78 range. It sold 980,000,000 Class A shares, raising about $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record. Shares were due to begin trading on Nasdaq as ANT on 19 November. Reported valuation is about $1.5 trillion.
sections.differing: Totals differ by source: $81.3bn for the IPO alone, versus about $107bn including a private placement, as Semafor and Newsweek report.
sections.unknown: First-day trading price and close were not available at drafting. Lock-up terms and the 30-day underwriter option's exercise are not yet reported.

analysis.title: Public exploit code follows fast
analysis.text: NGINX2Root, Cisco Expressway, Puppet and Java4Shell all had public proof-of-concept code or leaks around disclosure. Only Puppet and Roller have exploitation confirmed by an authority or vendor; the Cisco exploitation claim comes from a Russian vendor while Cisco's advisory says it knows of none.
